title: Code coverage: what it measures and what it does not

videos.script: Coverage answers one question exactly. Which lines did no test run? {{question}} People ask it a different question. Are the tests any good? It cannot answer that one, and this lesson shows why, with shipquote's own numbers. {{numbers}} You will read a coverage report line by line. Some files are at a hundred percent. One class is missing entirely, because its only tests were skipped. {{report}} Then the gap between ran and checked. A test file that asserts nothing reaches a hundred percent of the money module, and stays green when the code is broken. {{gap}} To measure the tests themselves, you will break the code on purpose, eight times. Six of the changes are caught. Two survive, in a file the report calls fully covered. {{mutants}} Then the rule a team is tempted to write. Fail the build below some percentage. You will watch the rule pass with a pipe in the way, and then pass again after two tests that check nothing. {{target}} The lesson ends with the readings that do help. Coverage of the lines a change added, and reports from several runs put back together. {{useful}}
